Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.

source.label: OpenStreetMap license-plate cameras (as mapped by DeFlock)

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Hemlock Township Police Department operates one drone as of 2019, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College.

Left out: other financing sources ($253,697) and uses ($64,470), such as transfers between the municipality's own funds and borrowing, which the statewide report does not break down.
"Other expenditures" ($64,746, mostly insurance, pensions and employee benefits) are spread across departments in proportion to their size.
Political money is not scored: Pennsylvania municipal candidates file campaign reports with their county board of elections, and there is no statewide database of those filings.
Cameras: no license-plate cameras are mapped inside Sugarloaf Township's borders in OpenStreetMap as of 2026-10-20.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Pennsylvania yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

Transparency: Sugarloaf Township has filed its annual audit and financial report with the Department of Community and Economic Development for FY 2025, the latest year most PA governments have filed. This is a check that the report was filed, not an opinion on its contents. The other five practices have not been checked yet, so they are left out of the score.
